question: Does the publicly accessible Bulacan State University student manuscript provide a usable Pantabangan freshwater inventory, and is it the same dataset as the 2026 journal article or 2013 GenBank submission?

sourceDocument.title: Profiling the invasive ichthyofaunal species of Pantabangan Dam through DNA barcoding
sourceDocument.affiliationAsPrinted: Department of Biology, College of Science, Bulacan State University
sourceDocument.documentDateNote: The file does not state a completion, defense, acceptance, or publication date or version. A dated 2024 student-grant progress post by lead author April Mae Linsangan Mangahas identifies the same project by title and research aim.
sourceDocument.hostStatus: The file is publicly readable from a third-party QR CDN. No matching official Bulacan State University repository record or item-specific reuse license was located in this bounded review.
sourceDocument.reviewAccess: PDF text reviewed in the browser. No local PDF copy, sequence strings, supplementary image files, or new raw data are retained.

projectContinuity.finding: The 2024 progress post is written by April Mae Linsangan Mangahas, names the Pantabangan DNA-barcode thesis project, and reports 41 fish from its first wet-season collection on 31 August to 1 September across three fishing locations and two tributaries, with dry-season sampling planned for January. The later manuscript lists Mangahas as first author, reports an August 2024-January 2025 collection period and 43 specimens across five named sites. This supports continuity of the student project; it does not provide a specimen-code crosswalk between the progress post and manuscript.
projectContinuity.confidence: project-level continuity supported; individual sample lineage not verified

studyScope.siteSelection: Three fishing locations (Barangay Villarica, Barangay Liberty, and Intang Lake) and two tributary sites (Barangay Conversion and Dilacay under Barangay Cadaclan), all described by the manuscript as within Pantabangan Dam.
studyScope.siteAllocation: The manuscript reports a total count per site, but this review does not republish the five-row site-count table. The site labels do not establish coordinates, a verified tributary-waterbody crosswalk, or a full-reservoir coverage boundary.
studyScope.samplingDesign: The manuscript describes samples obtained from fishers/market sampling and says at most three to five specimens per species per area were collected; samples below that minimum were retained as presence evidence. Counts are sample totals, not effort-standardized abundance, population estimates, or a complete checklist.
studyScope.dateAndCoordinateLimits: Only the overall field period was found. No specimen-to-day matrix, row-level coordinates, validated site geometry, or water-type classification was identified.

identificationAndFindings.methodsAsReported: COI barcoding, BLASTN, neighbor-joining analysis, K2P distances, and morphological, morphometric, and meristic comparison. The manuscript says amplicons were sequenced by Macrogen in South Korea.
identificationAndFindings.aggregateResultAsReported: The manuscript lists 14 taxon labels and 43 sample counts; it describes 12 as identified to species level by DNA barcoding and retains two provisional Micropterus cf. identifications based on morphology after molecular disagreement.
sourceInternalTaxonomyIssues: The three Micropterus samples are explicitly unresolved in the manuscript. One sample has a 100% BLASTN match to a GenBank reference but diverges in the neighbor-joining analysis; two others have low BLASTN similarity and do not resolve to the named species. Retain the cf. labels and do not admit species-level records from this source alone.

Zenarchopterus philippinus appears as a species-level result in the manuscript's table and abstract, while a discussion passage says morphological examination could only resolve it to genus because of missing references. Resolve this internal inconsistency before using the identity.
The manuscript calls four taxa new records for Pantabangan, but the reviewed source set does not establish a complete historical baseline against which novelty can be verified.

Invasive, native, endemic, beneficial, and conservation-status labels are literature-based interpretations in the manuscript. They are not adopted here and require separate current, taxon-specific verification.
identificationAndFindings.accessionInterpretation: The manuscript reports generating 43 COI sequences but no study-specific accession numbers or public deposit identifiers were located. Its Table 3 and Supplementary Data B list GenBank comparison/reference sequences used in BLAST or phylogenetic analysis; those reference accessions are not the manuscript's 43 new sample sequences.
identificationAndFindings.voucherTraceability: No collection accession numbers, museum repository deposit, or externally inspectable voucher crosswalk was found. Manuscript sample codes alone do not establish voucher custody.

crossSourceReconciliation.2024ProjectPost: The progress post and manuscript are strongly linked at project level by the student author, grant, thesis title/aim, wet-season sampling, and planned January dry-season return. The progress post's preliminary 41 fish and manuscript's final 43 specimens are not duplicate datasets to sum; no sample-code mapping was available.
crossSourceReconciliation.2026JournalArticle: The 2026 journal abstract reports 40 COI sequences and nine species. Its author list differs from this student manuscript. No shared voucher, accession, sequence, or specimen-code crosswalk is available, so overlap or independence remains unknown.
crossSourceReconciliation.2013NCBISubmission: The manuscript cites older Pantabangan GenBank records as comparison sequences. The NCBI review identified 40 earlier submitted fish records, mostly with explicit Pantabangan localities, but nothing in this student manuscript shows those earlier sequences are its own 43 samples.
crossSourceReconciliation.2015ClariasPaper: The 2015 Clarias analysis crosswalks five historical Pantabangan accessions; it does not verify the student manuscript's later specimens or the full 2026 article dataset.

reuseAndPublication.license: No item-specific open license or redistribution permission was found for the student manuscript, tables, figures, or specimen photographs.
reuseAndPublication.decision: Keep this as a cited research lead. Do not copy the manuscript's fish photographs, sequence data, complete taxon table, or derived invasiveness and novelty labels into Bangwit or its media assets.
reuseAndPublication.sequenceData: No sequence bases were transcribed or retained.
reuseAndPublication.appProjection: No app species rows, diets, fish images, occurrence points, geometry, safety guidance, or current-presence claims are approved.

nextStep: Locate an official institutional copy or thesis record and any project-sequence accession/voucher IDs; then verify item-specific reuse terms and review each taxon against independent taxonomy and specimen evidence. Continue to keep the student study separate from the 2026 journal article and older NCBI submissions until a row-level crosswalk is available.

sources.supports: Manuscript authors and affiliation, overall field period, five named sites, reported methods and aggregate results, accession/voucher limits, Micropterus ambiguity, Zenarchopterus inconsistency, and no reuse terms located.
Lead author's project identity, dated 2024 project context, preliminary wet-season sample count, site-group description, and planned dry-season sampling.
2026 journal abstract's reported 40 COI sequences, nine taxa, authors, and DOI.
2015 paper's separate five-accession Pantabangan Clarias analysis.
